source.excerpt: The greatest danger for most of us is not that our aim is too high and we miss it, but that it is too low and we reach it.
trail: Wikiquote labels the saying disputed and identifies its use without a source in Ken Robinson’s The Element. It also reports a related unattributed 1980 occurrence. Neither the original 1980 book nor Robinson’s printed page was independently inspected, so these remain reported leads rather than newly verified first appearances. Aim-high attribution warning ↗
Background on the historical artist; not evidence for this sentence. Who Michelangelo was ↗
